newsitem.title: MEXICO: Creditors grant Sidek new reprieve.
newsitem.headline: Creditors grant Sidek new reprieve.

text.p: Creditor banks have granted troubled holding company Grupo Sidek more time to come up with a long-awaited financial restructuring plan, a company director said on Tuesday.
"We have a new extension and negotiations continue," a Sidek director said by telephone, who asked not to be named.
"What I cannot tell you is when the new extension runs out," he added.
The latest in a series of extensions to time granted for reaching a restructuring agreement expired in June.

Mexican banks holding 70 percent of Sidek's debts agreed in 1996 to a standstill agreement in order not to demand debt payments and, at least temporarily, to waive their rights under Mexican law to seek the company's liquididation after it had posted negative equity.
